note: Majority: null. The Civil Code (Αστικός Κώδικας) article on full age was sought on 2026-10-31 and not read from a source the brief allows: the National Printing House's search (search.et.gr) answered behind a captcha, the private databases (kodiko.gr) did not show the article, lawspot.gr answered behind Cloudflare, and a web search for the article's words in Greek found no official text. Not modelled until read. Work: Law 1837/1989 'Για την προστασία των ανηλίκων κατά την απασχόληση' (ΦΕΚ 85/Α/23-3-1989), as published by ΕΛΙΝΥΑΕ (the Hellenic Institute for Occupational Health and Safety): art. 1 minors are those under 18; art. 2(1) minors who haven't completed their 15th year may not be employed in any work, save art. 3. This is the 1989 text; a later codification (Π.Δ. 62/2025, arts. 303-304, seen only on a private database in a search result) appears to carry the same rule, not read from an official copy. Performers: art. 3(1): with a permit of the Labour Inspectorate (άδεια της Επιθεώρησης Εργασίας), minors under 15 may be employed in theatre, music and other artistic events, advertising, fashion shows, radio and television, video and film, and as models, where their health and morals aren't harmed; art. 3(2) the permit is granted to the employer, names the child, the work and the daily schedule, and lasts at most three months; art. 3(3) the guardian's consent and a medical certificate are needed. No lowest age is set. Service: the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' consular page (Embassy in Chile, 'Στρατολογικά', read 2026-10-31) states Law 3421/2005 art. 1(1): every Greek citizen, from 1 January of the year he completes his 19th year until 31 December of the year he completes his 45th, must have completed military service, and all male Greek nationals file the census card in January and February of the year they reach their 19th year. In the year of turning 19 one is 18 for most of it, so the form holds from 18 (my reading of the calendar-year rule) until 45; it is men only ('άρρενες'). The length of service was not read from a source (a search found only a 2021 ministry reply giving the legal full obligation as 24 months, cut by ministerial decision; the army's own pages read gave none), so months is null. Women's service is voluntary, which the form doesn't hold.
